content.text: Still experiencing this problem with v4.5.1 final.
Is this issue going to be addressed?

I had an issue that manifested similarly.  In the full fedora logs there was a BROKEN PIPE exception and I worked with networking to try to address the issue.  We couldn't, but we found a workaround that was suitable as as stopgap until the Modeshape5-based fedora.
In our infinispan configuration we switched from a pool to a simple-connection....
<jdbc:simple-connection connection-url="jdbc:mysql://${fcrepo.ispn.mysql.host:localhost}:${fcrepo.ispn.mysql.port:3306}...
This prevented the idle timeouts.  It seems that the infinispan connection pooling doesn't validate connections so when one has timed out, you get an exception.  It didn't
appear
to corrupt the DB if it occurred during a write, but I couldn't be sure.

Not using pooling means that there's a new connection opened for every request.  This works in our case because our traffic is super light.  I can easily see how under heavy load this workaround would cause a different problem (running out of handles for not-yet-cleaned-up TCP connections to the database).
See simple-connection vs connection-pool here:
http://docs.jboss.org/infinispan/7.0/configdocs/infinispan-cachestore-jdbc-config-7.0.html
The 4.6.0 release should allow you to specify finer logging levels
for the ExceptionMapper implementations (in this case, I expect it's WildcardExceptionMapper) to see the rest of the stacktrace.
We need to see a little more about the issue to sort out whether this is something we have any control over, or whether it's a mariaDB and/or ISPN problem.
Just chiming in that I experienced this issue on a fresh installation of Fedora 4.6.0 (with RBACL).
Environment: CentOS 7, Tomcat 7.0.54, Oracle Java 1.8u101, PostgreSQL 8.4.20
I tried configuring a JNDI JDBC connection as noted here:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA46/Configuring+JDBC+Object+Store
but that ultimately resulted in the same errors.
